prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Extreme · 10 columns + unbreakable values (language en).
Grid: 10 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 16px
  col 2: header "SKU" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 136px
  col 3: header "Color" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "Size" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "Qty" · longest unbreakable word 26px · one-line width 26px
  col 6: header "Price" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 7: header "Tax" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 8: header "Total" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 9: header "Warehouse" · longest unbreakable word 81px · one-line width 122px
  col 10: header "Tracking" · longest unbreakable word 159px · one-line width 159px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"An order or inventory line-item table linking product variants and quantities to prices, warehouse locations and shipment tracking.","reading":"Readers scan each row across to connect a product with its quantity, cost and fulfillment details, and compare quantities and monetary amounts down their columns. On a phone, horizontal scrolling separates the first visible product fields from later fulfillment fields.","groups":["ID and SKU identify each line item; Color and Size describe the product variant.","Qty, Price, Tax and Total describe the quantity and financial amounts, which readers compare across rows.","Warehouse and Tracking describe fulfillment and shipment; both are needed to locate or follow an order. "],"keep_intact":["SKU segments and tracking identifiers are most useful when readable without arbitrary character splits.","IDs, quantities, sizes and monetary amounts should stay intact for reliable scanning.","Color names and the Warehouse and Tracking headers should stay intact when space permits."],"may_wrap":["SKU values may wrap at existing hyphens if the browser permits, though keeping each SKU on one line is easier to scan.","Multiword warehouse values may wrap at word spaces; the resulting row height can also accommodate natural SKU wrapping."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:

Design r0C: widths [38, 51, 38, 38, 38, 38, 38, 38, 45, 50] · table 413×611px · row heights [106, 176, 176, 153] · column headers wrapped 9/10 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 60 · OVERFLOWS the box by 53px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
